library(targets)

## Methods

### Study Sites

The experiment was conducted at twelve semi-natural grassland sites in the Vestland Climate Grid (VCG) in south-western Norway. The sites were selected along three temperature (boreal, sub-alpine, and alpine) and four precipitation levels. The gradients ranged from 6.5°C to 10.5°C growing season temperatures and mean annual precipitation varying from 600 mm to 2600 mm. Apart from differing in mean growing season temperature and annual precipitation, the sites were selected to be as similar as possible in grazing regime and history, bedrock, vegetation type and structure, slope and exposure. For more details on the study site and experimental design see @vandvik2022role.

### Experimental Design

To assess the effects of plant functional group removals on standing biomass and community composition, we set up a fully factorial plant functional group removal experiment in 2015. We focused on the dominant plant functional groups including graminoids (G; grasses, sedges, and rushes), forbs (F; including herbaceous forbs, pteridophytes, dwarf-shrubs, and small individuals of trees and shrubs), and bryophytes (B; including mosses, liverworts, and hornworts). At each site, eight 25 x 25 cm plots were established and replicated four times (32 plots per site and n = 384 plots in total). Within each block we randomly assigned the removal treatments of the three plant functional groups and all possible combination resulting in eight treatments: control (intact vegetation), three single functional group removals, three pairwise removals, and complete removal of all three functional groups (bare ground; Figure).

The removals were done annually at peak growing season between 2015 and 2022. In 2016 and 2017, the removals were done twice, including a removal in the spring. The above ground biomass of the relevant plant functional group(s) were removed. The below ground biomass, litter and lichens were left intact.

![Experimental design. A) Location or study sites and showing the sites within the climate grid (temperature and precipitation gradients). B) Removal treatments and data collection for plant species composition. C) Timeline showing the functional group removal and data collection on vascular plant composition. (Panel C needs to be reduced to 2 first lines!).](exp_design.png)

### Data Collection

#### Above ground biomass (removed and remaining)

Above ground biomass was collected annually from all experimental plots. The biomass was harvested for each plot, separating each functional group (graminoids, forbs, bryophytes), drying it to constant mass at 60°C and weighing.

In 2022, the whole experiment was harvested and the above ground biomass from all plant functional groups in all plots was removed. The biomass was also dried at 60°C and weighed. The biomass from the plant functional groups from the removal treatments is hereafter called *removed biomass*. The biomass from the remaining plant functional groups is hereafter called *standing biomass*.

#### Root biomass

Root biomass was harvested in 2022 from the edge of each plot using ingrowth cores installed in 2021 (g m^3^). (why the edge?). The cores were washed and sieved, and the roots retrieved and weighed to calculated their wet mass. They were then freeze dried to calculate root biomass and root dry matter content (dry root biomass/wet root biomass). See FUNDER paper for further details.

#### Plant Community Composition

Plant community composition recorded annually between 2015 and 2019 across all experimental plots. We recorded the presence and visually estimated the cover of each species per plot.

### Data preparation

### Analysis


Using *standing biomass* in 2022 (remaining biomass after removal).

Calculate two functional group removal treatments:

- functional group richness (number of functional group present: 0, 1, 2, 3)

- factorial functional group remaining

```{r}
#| label: tbl-removal-treatments
#| tbl-cap: "Factorial functional group removal treatments"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

tar_load(standing_biomass_22_wide)

standing_biomass_22_wide |>
  distinct(fg_removed, G_treat, F_treat, B_treat) |>
  mutate(
    n_groups_removed = G_treat + F_treat + B_treat,
    removal = factor(
      fg_removed,
      levels = c("none", "G", "F", "B", "GF", "GB", "FB"),
      labels = c(
        "None",
        "Graminoids",
        "Forbs",
        "Bryophytes",
        "Graminoids + forbs",
        "Graminoids + bryophytes",
        "Forbs + bryophytes"
      )
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(n_groups_removed, removal) |>
  select(removal, G_treat, F_treat, B_treat) |>
  gt() |>
  cols_label(
    removal = "Removal",
    G_treat = "Graminoids",
    F_treat = "Forbs",
    B_treat = "Bryophytes"
  )
```

**PART 1: Community analysis**

**Functional group richness:** compare full model with 2-way interaction model

To test how functional group richness (i.e. number of remaining functional groups) affects standing biomass, we ran a Gaussian glmmTMB models with standing biomass as response and functional group richness, temperature and precipitation as predictors. Block nested within site (`1|siteID/blockID`) was used as random effect. Temperature and precipitation were scaled. We compared the full model with all interactions to the two-way interaction model (see below).

*Full model*: standing biomass \~ fg_richness \* precipitation_scaled \* temperature_scaled + (1\|siteID/blockID)

*2-way model*: standing biomass \~ fg_richness + precipitation_scaled + temperature_scaled + fg_richness:precipitation_scaled + fg_richness:temperature_scaled + precipitation_scaled:temperature_scaled + (1\|siteID/blockID)

**Factorial functional group:** 

Due to limited power, only 2-way interactions are considered for the factorial functional group analysis.

How does functional group removal affect standing biomass:\
**Response**: total standing biomass\
**Predictor**: FG removed x climate

```{r}
#| label: full-model
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mod_B_comp <- glmmTMB(
  total_biomass ~
    # main effects
  F_treat +
  B_treat +
  B_treat +
  temperature_scaled +
  precipitation_scaled +
    # treatment interations
  G_treat:F_treat +
  G_treat:B_treat +
  F_treat:B_treat +
    #climate interaction
  temperature_scaled:precipitation_scaled +
    #climate and treatment interactions
  G_treat:temperature_scaled +
  G_treat:precipitation_scaled +
  F_treat:temperature_scaled +
  F_treat:precipitation_scaled +
  B_treat:temperature_scaled +
  B_treat:precipitation_scaled +
  (1 | siteID/blockID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = standing_biomass_22_wide
)
```

*Contrasts*: to test for the effect of each functional group on the above-ground biomass quantities alone and in combination with other functional groups along both climate gradients, we compare each single-presence treatment with the control plot, and 

**PART 2: Functional group analysis**

For subset of functional group remaining, i.e. here only described for plots where bryophytes are present:\
**Response** = bryophyte biomass\
**Predictors** = the *other* two removals (`G_treat`, `F_treat`) × climate\

```{r}
#| label: bryophyte-model
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mod_B_comp <- glmmTMB(
  B ~
    # main effects
    G_treat +
    F_treat +
    temperature_scaled +
    precipitation_scaled +
    # treatment interaction
    G_treat:F_treat +
    # climate interaction
    temperature_scaled:precipitation_scaled +
    # treatment and climate interactions
    G_treat:F_treat:temperature_scaled +
    G_treat:F_treat:precipitation_scaled +
    (1 | siteID/blockID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = B_comp_dat
)
```

**Testing for climate and functional group effects**
Main effects of the above model, replicated for forbs and graminoids, are extracted from the model summary.
To dig deeper into the climate-dependent contrasts, and the effects of each functional group's presence on the above-ground biomass of the target functional group (bryophytes in the example above), we computed estimated marginal means from the fitted models using the `emmeans` package. Group means of the treatments and control were then compared along each climate gradient, once for temperature (precipitation kept constant) and once for precipitation (temperature kept constant).

A description of the pairwise comparisons can be found below:

|               | **F remains** | **F removed** |
|---------------|:--------------|:--------------|
| **G remains** | control       | F removal     |
| **G removed** | G removal     | GF removal    |


*Primary contrasts (functional group vs control):*
To test for the primary effects of  contrasts of G removal, F removal, and GF removal versus control (neither G nor F removed).

\
*Does functional group removal depend on other functional groups:*

What is the extra effect of adding G removal on top of F removal or vice versa:

- GF vs F only

- GF vs G only

Is the effect of removing one FG the same as when the other group is still present? (interaction)

- Effect of removing G when F is kept: `G − control`

- Effect of removing G when F is already gone: `GF − F`

- Does removal of G depend on F: `(GF − F) − (G − control)`\

```{r}
#| label: fig-factorial-comparisons-overview
#| fig-cap: "Contrasts among functional group treatments for the bryophyte-present model illustrated above. Each row corresponds to a contrast, each column to an experimental treatment. Functional groups present at the end of the experiment are shown in full colour, those that have been experimentallly removed are washed out. The bottom row represents the `(GF − F) − (G − control)` contrast."
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

tar_read(factorial_comparisons_overview)
```


**PART 3: Below-ground biomass analysis**

How does functional group removal affect belowground biomass:\
**Response**: root biomass (g m^3^)\
**Predictor**: FG removed x climate

Since the roots are pooled across functional groups, our model is simpler:
```{r}
#| label: root-biomass-model
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

mod_root_biomass <- glmmTMB(
  root_biomass ~
    # main effects
  F_treat +
  B_treat +
  B_treat +
  temperature_scaled +
  precipitation_scaled +
    # treatment interations
  G_treat:F_treat +
  G_treat:B_treat +
  F_treat:B_treat +
    #climate interaction
  temperature_scaled:precipitation_scaled +
    #climate and treatment interactions
  G_treat:temperature_scaled +
  G_treat:precipitation_scaled +
  F_treat:temperature_scaled +
  F_treat:precipitation_scaled +
  B_treat:temperature_scaled +
  B_treat:precipitation_scaled +
  (1 | siteID/blockID),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = root_biomass
)
```
